_note: SOC-100 Scenario Corpus · investigation-guidance layer.  Never detection, never evidence-state, never verdict.  Scenarios describe what to LOOK FOR, never what HAPPENED.

scenarios.name: Spoofed Microsoft 365 Password Reset
scenarios.threat: Attacker impersonates the identity team to harvest credentials via a look-alike sign-in portal.
scenarios.initial_observable: SEG flags a message impersonating identity team linking to a look-alike sign-in portal.
scenarios.next_step: Correlate the initial alert with identity sign-ins, MFA prompts, and token issuance.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Combine email gateway alerts with identity sign-in telemetry.

scenarios.name: BEC Reply-Chain Hijack
scenarios.threat: Attacker hijacks a legitimate email conversation to request fraudulent payment instructions.
scenarios.initial_observable: A trusted supplier conversation suddenly contains revised payment instructions from the same thread.
scenarios.next_step: Compare historic sender infrastructure, Reply-To values, writing pattern and message headers with prior legitimate messages.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Detect suspicious changes in email threads or unusual payment requests.

scenarios.name: EDR Blocks Unknown Executable
scenarios.threat: EDR detects an unsigned executable launched from the user Downloads directory, indicating potential malware execution.
scenarios.initial_observable: EDR blocks an unsigned executable launched from the user Downloads directory.
scenarios.next_step: Confirm EDR disposition, detection time, host, user, file/process path and whether the object was blocked, quarantined, merely detected or actually executed.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Hunt for file hashes, filenames, certificates, and behavioral indicators enterprise-wide.

scenarios.name: Word Spawns Suspicious Child Process
scenarios.threat: Microsoft Word creates a cmd.exe process which then makes a network connection, suggesting malicious code execution.
scenarios.initial_observable: EDR detects WINWORD.EXE creating cmd.exe followed by a network connection.
scenarios.next_step: Capture process tree and document path/hash.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Correlate outbound connections with file creation and subsequent persistence.

scenarios.name: Impossible Travel Sign-in
scenarios.threat: A single user account authenticates from geographically-distant locations within a short window, indicating stolen credentials or session replay.
scenarios.initial_observable: Identity provider reports authentications from geographically-distant locations within a short time window.
scenarios.next_step: Verify device metadata, VPN attribution and MFA behaviour on each sign-in before treating as compromise.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Correlate impossible-travel with device fingerprints and privileged-action telemetry.

scenarios.name: MFA Fatigue / Push Bombing
scenarios.threat: Repeated MFA push prompts sent to a user account, aiming to coerce an approval and take over the session.
scenarios.initial_observable: Identity provider records a burst of MFA push prompts for a single account.
scenarios.next_step: Determine if any push prompt was approved and what session followed.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Trigger identity risk scoring on MFA-prompt bursts and force re-auth with number-matching.

scenarios.name: VPN Access from Anonymising Infrastructure
scenarios.threat: A corporate VPN account connects from a known proxy / Tor exit / hosting provider, indicating credential theft or evasion.
scenarios.initial_observable: VPN concentrator records a session originating from a known anonymising IP range.
expected_evidence: abnormal user role for source geography
scenarios.next_step: Assess device posture at connect time and correlate with post-connect actions.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Enrich VPN sign-ins with real-time anonymiser and hosting-range intel.

scenarios.name: Split-Tunnel Exfiltration
scenarios.threat: A VPN-connected endpoint uploads a large volume of data to a personal cloud service using the split-tunnel egress.
scenarios.initial_observable: Endpoint DLP records a large personal-cloud upload while a corporate VPN session is active.
scenarios.next_step: Quantify volume, file sensitivity and destination before invoking DLP response.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Correlate split-tunnel egress with data-classification telemetry.

scenarios.name: DNS Tunnelling Signature
scenarios.threat: Repeated long / high-entropy TXT / NULL queries to a controlled domain suggest DNS tunnelling for C2 or exfiltration.
scenarios.initial_observable: Passive DNS records high-volume long-label queries to a low-reputation domain.
scenarios.next_step: Attribute the queries to a specific host + process before blocking.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Baseline query-length distribution per domain and alert on outliers.

scenarios.name: DGA Beaconing
scenarios.threat: An endpoint queries a rotating set of algorithmically-generated domains, indicative of DGA-based C2.
scenarios.initial_observable: Passive DNS shows an endpoint querying many high-entropy sub-domains within a short window.
expected_evidence: consistent NXDOMAIN followed by 1 successful resolution
scenarios.next_step: Pivot from the successful resolution to the connecting process + subsequent outbound activity.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Enable DGA-scoring on high-entropy FQDN queries.

scenarios.name: PowerShell With EncodedCommand
scenarios.threat: PowerShell is launched with an EncodedCommand argument, hiding the underlying script from casual log review.
scenarios.initial_observable: EDR / Sysmon records powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand and a large base64 argument.
scenarios.next_step: Decode the argument; distinguish CAPABILITY of the decoded content from what actually executed.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Correlate encoded PowerShell with script-block logs and subsequent EDR events.

scenarios.name: PowerShell Downloads Then Executes
scenarios.threat: PowerShell performs a network fetch and immediately executes the downloaded content, a classic stager pattern.
scenarios.initial_observable: Script-block logs show Invoke-WebRequest / IEX / DownloadString followed by execution.
scenarios.next_step: Retrieve the downloaded content out-of-band and analyse its capability; then confirm what actually ran.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Alert on IEX / DownloadString / Invoke-WebRequest patterns in script-block logs.

scenarios.name: Shadow Copy Deletion
scenarios.threat: vssadmin / wmic is used to delete volume shadow copies, a common pre-encryption step in ransomware.
scenarios.initial_observable: Process telemetry shows vssadmin delete shadows or wmic shadowcopy delete.
scenarios.next_step: Correlate the deletion command with concurrent file-encryption / rename activity.
scenarios.detection_improvement: High-fidelity alert on any vssadmin delete / wmic shadowcopy delete.

scenarios.name: Mass File Rename / Extension Change
scenarios.threat: High-frequency file renames with a common suffix appear across a share, indicating active ransomware encryption.
scenarios.initial_observable: File-server audit records thousands of renames with the same new extension.
scenarios.next_step: Contain the originating host immediately and preserve evidence before rollback.
scenarios.detection_improvement: High-fidelity rate-based alert on identical-suffix rename bursts.

scenarios.name: New Owner Added to Cloud Application
scenarios.threat: A newly-created principal is added as owner of a critical cloud application, indicating consent-phish or admin abuse.
scenarios.initial_observable: Cloud audit records an OwnerAdd action on a first-party application.
scenarios.next_step: Verify actor's normal privilege baseline and reverse the owner change if unauthorised.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Alert on OwnerAdd for any application in the crown-jewel list.

scenarios.name: IAM Key Created for Existing User
scenarios.threat: A new IAM access key is created for an existing user by another identity, commonly used to persist access after a compromise.
scenarios.initial_observable: Cloud CloudTrail-equivalent shows CreateAccessKey for a user, executed by a different principal.
expected_evidence: immediate API use of the new key
scenarios.next_step: Correlate the new key with downstream API calls before rotating.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Alert on CreateAccessKey where actor ≠ target and outside approved windows.

scenarios.name: Bulk Repository Clone Before Resignation
scenarios.threat: A user clones many private repositories shortly before HR-flagged departure, indicating potential source-code theft.
scenarios.initial_observable: Repository audit shows a burst of clones by a single user close to their resignation date.
scenarios.next_step: Record observable facts (files, timestamps, destinations) without assigning motive; engage insider-risk / HR / legal channels.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Detect abnormal repository-clone volume correlated with HR departure signals.

scenarios.name: Repeated Security Policy Bypass Attempts
scenarios.threat: A user repeatedly disables endpoint controls, uses unauthorised tools, or bypasses web restrictions.
scenarios.initial_observable: Endpoint telemetry records repeated control-change attempts from the same user / host.
scenarios.next_step: Record observable facts; escalate through defined insider-risk / governance channels rather than confronting the user independently.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Escalate policy-bypass attempts through insider-risk governance.

scenarios.name: SQL Injection Attempt Against Internet Portal
scenarios.threat: WAF detects SQL injection payload patterns in requests to a public application.
scenarios.initial_observable: WAF records SQL-injection-like payloads against a public application.
scenarios.next_step: Capture the inbound request end-to-end (source, method, URI, headers, parameters, timestamp, WAF rule / action).  Distinguish attempted vs successful.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Correlate WAF blocks with application errors and database queries.

scenarios.name: WAF Block Followed by Host Compromise Indicators
scenarios.threat: WAF blocks repeated exploit requests, but EDR later alerts on the same web server, indicating a potential web shell or host compromise.
scenarios.initial_observable: WAF blocks repeated exploit requests, but EDR later alerts on the same web server.
expected_evidence: later EDR alert on same host
process / file creation coincident with earlier requests
scenarios.next_step: Merge WAF, application and EDR events into a single timeline before concluding compromise.
scenarios.detection_improvement: Identify process / file creation and privilege changes on the server to confirm compromise path.
